ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD under CMF Art. L.561-5; systematic electronic screening of all UBOs, the gerant, and the corporate counter-party against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated list, French DG Tresor restrictive-measures list, and OFAC SDN list (required for USD-denominated Wire rails); PEP status determination per CMF Art. L.561-10; multi-layered source-of-funds verification for any capital injection above EUR 10,000; Tracfin STR filing for any unexplained inconsistency.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalites des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated jointly by INPI and the RCS; availability pre-search via Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) on the National RCS database; complementary INPI trademark database search (data.inpi.fr).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be renderable in Latin-script characters for registration and searchability in the RCS; non-Latin script denominations (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic) require a verified Latin transliteration. The name may be in French or a foreign language, but must not contravene public order (Loi Toubon No. 94-665 of 4 Aug 1994) and must be accompanied by a French-language corporate name in all statutory filings.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Avocat / Notaire / Commissaire aux comptes (regulated professions; bar membership required)
France / Republique / Ministere / Prefecture (misleading official implication; special ministerial approval)
Universite / Ecole / College (misleading educational status; ministerial approval)
S.A. / S.A.S. / S.A.R.L. tokens inconsistent with actual corporate form or intended partner count
Police / Gendarmerie / National (usurpation of public authority)
Societe de gestion / Fonds (AMF license connotation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide a formal statutory name-reservation mechanism at the RCS; the 30-day parameter corresponds to (i) the recommended INPI trademark-awareness priority window and (ii) the customary period within which an identical or confusingly similar name risk must be cleared before filing. If the greffier rejects the name at incorporation, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal (refus d'immatriculation) via the Guichet unique; the applicant may immediately amend the articles of association and resubmit the formation file without an administrative appeal. If the registrar maintains the refusal, a petition (requete) may be filed with the president of the competent commercial court within one month of notification (Code de commerce, RCS refusal recusal procedure); a parallel appeal against an INPI trademark refusal lies with the Cour d'appel within one month (Art. L.411-4, Code de la propriete intellectuelle).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk services ODC under Art. L.123-11-2, Code de commerce through a licensed domiciliation provider (societe de domiciliation) or a business centre; a pure mail-forwarding address without physical receptacle and director meeting facilities is not compliant. The domiciliation contract must be annexed to the statutes and filed with the RCS; the registered office must be able to receive service of process and provide access to accounting records for tax inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very Low (approximately 2-5% annualized for a low-risk ODC with no in-house French staff); no systematic pre-incorporation premises visit; physical verification occurs mainly upon announced tax audit (verification de comptabilite) and ad hoc URSSAF labour controls if French employees are later onboarded; the domiciliation must therefore maintain an auditable physical presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general commercial companies), L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL) and related implementing regulations R.123-135 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS), administered by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce and operated through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Official online application for registration of a societe commerciale (legacy Cerfa M0 / demande d'immatriculation au RCS) accompanied by the signed statuts and all statutory annexes
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; the SARL may be formed with freely determined capital, typically EUR 1. Under Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code, at least one-fifth of cash contributions must be paid at incorporation and the full subscribed cash capital must be deposited in a blocked bank account with an attestation de depot des fonds until RCS registration; funds are released to the company after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the capital subscription of EUR [•], divided into [•] equal shares, as set out in the signed Articles of Association, is hereby ratified and accepted; that cash contributions shall be lodged with a regulated bank and released in compliance with Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code; that the registered office is adopted at the address stated in the Articles; that [•] is appointed Gérant with full powers of administration and representation; and that the Gérant is instructed to publish the legal announcement and complete the registration of the company on the RCS through the Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Signing and Optional Notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Data database for name verification; notary public if notarization is chosen or required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed company name against RCS/INPI records; prepare French-language SARL statuts containing the corporate name, corporate object, registered office address, share capital, share distribution, profit allocation, manager provisions and duration; have all partners sign the statuts and the nomination of the Gérant; if real estate is contributed or if the partners so choose, execute the documents before a notary; retain one original set for the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts
Nomination of Gérant
Power of attorney of any agent signatory
Identity documents of all partners and the manager
INPI/RCS name search report (advisory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the corporate object, amend the statuts by supplementary agreement to a precise ISIC 6202 software-engineering wording and re-sign before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Account and Deposit of Cash Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regulated credit institution under Banque de France supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company 'in formation'; deposit the agreed cash capital; ask the bank to issue an attestation de depot des fonds specifying the company name, deposited amount and account details; instruct the bank to release the funds only upon presentation of the RCS Kbis or official registration certificate; attach the attestation to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Draft or signed statuts
Identity documents and proof of address for each signatory
Initial deposit funds
Source-of-funds evidence and bank KYC questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC documents, provide passport scans, beneficial-ownership statements and source-of-funds bank statements; if the bank refuses, select another regulated bank and obtain a fresh attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice in an Authorized Announcement Journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces legales habilite in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the 'avis de constitution' to an approved legal-announcement newspaper in the department where the registered office is situated; include the legal form, share capital, registered office address, corporate object, manager identity and RCS court; pay the publication fee and obtain the attestation de parution confirming the publication date and text.
required_dossiers: Avis de constitution text signed by the Gérant
Extract of the purposes and partners from the statuts
Order form and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication text is incomplete or erroneous, request a corrected republication or an addendum; confirm the journal's habilitation before payment; retain the final justificatif for the RCS file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Incorporation File to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the official portal, select 'creation d'une societe commerciale - SARL', complete the dynamic form in French, upload all required PDF documents, pay the official INPI/RCS filing fee and submit the application electronically; the portal sends an acknowledgement and routes the file to the Greffe, INSEE, tax authorities and social-security authorities.
required_dossiers: Online registration form / Cerfa M0 declaration
Signed statuts and annexes
Attestation de depot des fonds
Justificatif de parution of the legal announcement
Declaration on honour of non-condamnation for each manager
Identity document and proof of address of each manager
Declaration of beneficial owners
Power of attorney if a third party signs the application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is flagged incomplete, correct the dossier through the same portal within the INPI electronic deadline, typically 15 working days; upload missing documents or rectified statuts; if refused, request the reasoned refusal and submit a revised application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Adjudication, Kbis Issuance and INSEE Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Registre du commerce et des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the legal compliance of the file, registers the SARL on the RCS, and notifies INSEE, BODACC and accompanying authorities; after registration, obtain the official Kbis extract, SIREN number, SIRET number and APE/NACE code; verify that the managing director, registered office and corporate object are correctly recorded and obtain certified copies for banking and contractual purposes.
required_dossiers: Complete application forwarded by INPI
INPI/RCS fee payment receipt
Copy of the legal announcement justificatif
Identity verification and beneficial-ownership declaration already submitted in Step 4
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe refuses registration, it must state the grounds; cure the defect by filing a rectificatif or supplementary act, pay any additional taxes if applicable, and refile; if the refusal persists, apply to the judge supervising the RCS for review within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable; software-engineering and offshore development center activities under ISIC 6202 do not require an industrial license from the Direction Generale des Entreprises or any industrial board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate operating or manufacturing permit required; the SARL obtains only RCS/Kbis registration, INSEE identifiers and standard business formalities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de la Transition ecologique et de la Cohesion des territoires; regional DREAL where physical premises are established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for software-engineering office activities; no ICPE installation classee is operated and no EIA is triggered under Article R.122-2 of the Environmental Code for ISIC 6202.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operations must comply with municipal waste separation obligations, electrical and electronic equipment (DEEE) take-back rules under Articles R.543-172 et seq., and general Code de l'environnement duties for waste management; no industrial wastewater or VOC discharge permit is required; any cleaning-agent VOCs remain within Labour Code workplace thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For leased professional office space, the landlord must provide the building fire-safety certificate and the SARL must maintain extinguishers, emergency exits, evacuation plans and workplace fire-prevention measures under the Labour Code and applicable ERP regulations; if the premises are open to the public, obtain the Commission de securite approval; no structural load certificate is required for ordinary office use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — impots.gouv.fr; customs and cross-border goods formalities: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) — douane.gouv.fr; business registry and SIREN issuance: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (INPI) — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must register for French VAT and obtain a French TIN before making its first taxable supply in France. The application is submitted to the DGFiP through the online business formalities portal (Guichet Unique) or to the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) using form Cerfa n°10456*08 for the régime réel d'imposition. Non-EU/EEA-established foreign companies must appoint a tax representative in France accredited under Article 202 of the French General Tax Code (CGI). Upon approval, INSEE issues a SIREN identifier used as the French corporate TIN and a SIRET number for each establishment; VAT-specific intra-Community identifiers are then issued for cross-border transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at the entity level. A small SARL may elect under Article 239 bis AA CGI to be taxed as a pass-through entity at the personal income tax (impôt sur le revenu, IR) level for a maximum of five fiscal years, provided all shareholders are natural persons and the share capital is fully paid up and held under specific ownership conditions; the election is made with the competent tax office and applies to all partners. France does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; however, hybrid entity mismatches are adjusted via the ATAD implementation rules and tax residence is determined by place of effective management and registered office.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For French-established entities: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for supplies of goods; EUR 37,500 annual turnover for supplies of services. There is no registration threshold for foreign-established entities: any taxable operation in France triggers a French VAT registration obligation from the first euro. The general EU distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 applies only to intra-EU distance sales of goods; cross-border B2B services are generally taxed at the customer's place of establishment, not by the French threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory structured B2B electronic invoicing under the 2024 reform. From 1 September 2026, all established taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices, and large and medium-sized enterprises must issue e-invoices; from 1 September 2027, small and micro enterprises must also issue structured e-invoices. Invoicing and e-reporting data must be transmitted through an accredited Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF), using EN 16931-compliant formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII). There is no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control stamping, or pre-clearance API with the DGFiP for ordinary domestic invoices; however, customs export declarations must be filed electronically through the DGDDI's DELTA/GUS system. Cross-border B2B and B2C sales are subject to periodic e-reporting to the tax administration from the same implementation date.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the European Union qualify for a 0% VAT (exonération) under Article 262-I CGI if the goods physically leave France/EU territory within the statutory time limits (normally within three months, extendable to six months with justification) and the exporter holds probative evidence of export. Intra-EU dispatches to a taxable person are zero-rated provided the purchaser's valid VAT identification number is disclosed and the goods are transported to another Member State. Offshore software engineering and maintenance services supplied to a non-French business customer are treated as supplied where the customer is established under Article 259-1 CGI; the French supplier therefore applies 0% French VAT by excluding the services from French scope, provided it obtains documentary evidence that the customer is a taxable person acting as such (valid EU VAT ID or official foreign tax residence certificate, contract showing business customer status) and that the services are not physically performed for a fixed French establishment of the customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU) filed via DELTA/GUS with customs approval
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / transport document evidencing physical export)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of foreign exchange collection / bank transfer credit advice)
Commercial invoice bearing the zero-rating reference and the customer's VAT ID
Proof of exit from France/EU (e.g., Exit Summary Declaration, transport manifest, or carrier certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are rigorously audited by the DGFiP and DGDDI. If the requisite documentary evidence is missing or false, the French tax authority re-assesses the supply at the standard 20% French VAT, together with late-payment interest at 0.20% per month (CGI Art. 1731) and an additional penalty of 40% for serious tax misstatement or 80% for fraudulent behavior (CGI Art. 1729); an 80/50% penalty can apply for concealed operations. Criminal tax fraud penalties under Article 1741 CGI include fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Customs irregularities can trigger administrative fines and confiscation under Customs Code Articles 410 and 413. Refunds of input VAT are available when zero-rated exports are properly substantiated; unjustified refund claims trigger additional fines under Article 1788A CGI.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury); banking and payment supervision is delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. France applies EU capital movement liberalization; no prior foreign-exchange authorization is required for current or capital account transactions. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders require no exchange-control permit, provided they are supported by approved financial statements and shareholder distributions; dividends remain subject to French withholding tax unless treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief applies. Banks must report transaction-level data to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics on payments above €50,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds in France. Exporters may hold EUR or foreign currency abroad and in French accounts; however, statistical balance-of-payments reporting to Banque de France applies to individual external transactions equal to or exceeding €50,000. No conversion ratios exist.

Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) / Operational Account (Compte Courant)
Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) / Operational Account (Compte Courant)
Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) / Operational Account (Compte Courant)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for EU-licensed electronic money institutions (e.g., Wise Europe, Payoneer Europe) passporting into France under EEA e-money and payment-services legislation; low viability for offshore non-EU EMIs because they may not accept client deposits or operate without an EU branch/passport. Such platforms are recommended only for operational disbursements, not for statutory capital escrow or principal clearing relationships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a blanket statutory mandate for a physical interview; banks may permit remote onboarding through certified video identification and electronic KYC portals. In practice, French tier-1 banks often require at least one in-person or video meeting for non-resident directors/UBOs, especially where ultimate ownership is overseas. A notarized power of attorney or a face-to-face visit is frequently demanded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident individual UBO/manager with no French tax or social footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport or national ID; proof of residential address; tax residence certificate; extract of UBO register; corporate authorization/shareholder resolution; banker's reference from the originating jurisdiction; negative-media and sanctions screening explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore development centre with substantial revenue from a single related-party foreign parent
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreement with granular scope; time-and-effort records; delivery evidence (source-code repository logs, tickets, reviews); invoices and proof of settlement; arm's-length transfer-pricing study; audited financial statements; French employment contracts and payroll/URSSAF declarations for local staff.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border inbound transactions not clearly matched to invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client-specific contracts, statement of work, project milestones, goods/services description, purpose codes, bank ledger reconciliation, and sub-ledger ageing reports; management letters and legal opinion confirming the offshore service model; UBO and shareholder structure chart.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Injections from the non-resident parent to the French SARL should be routed via SWIFT MT103 / SEPA or SWIFT internal transfer to the designated capital escrow account, using the European balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment and the narrative 'augmentation de capital' for equity or 'avance en compte courant d'associé' for shareholder loans. Supporting documents include: Kbis extract, shareholder meeting minutes, board resolution, capital subscription deed, and certified identity/UBO documents. Projections in EUR: if funds arrive in foreign currency, the receiving bank executes EUR conversion at current market price; no separate French FX authorization is needed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade settlements should use SWIFT MT103 for supplier invoices, SWIFT MT202 COV for correspondent-bank cover payments, and SEPA Credit Transfer / Instant SEPA within the EEA. Commercial letters of credit should be issued as irrevocable documentary credits under UCP600 for import settlements, with standby L/Cs where security is required. All messages must carry full originator/beneficiary details and an accurate purpose code to enable KYC and sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for fully unconvertible or exotic currency exposures, subject to bank credit approval and EMIR margining

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts and Tax Return (Comptes Annuels et Liasse Fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Commercial Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) and French Tax Authorities (Direction des Services Fiscaux)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 4 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from €1,500 to €7,500 for late filing; administrative strike-off possible after 3 months of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Capital exceeding €800,000 or turnover exceeding €800,000 or total assets exceeding €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update of UBO information required if shareholding or beneficial ownership changes during the year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate applicable to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2022; reduced 15% band on first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit available to qualifying SMEs)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; preferential provisions include French R&D tax credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche) at 30% and Innovation Tax Credit at 20% within statutory caps, SME reduced corporate income tax band at 15%, patent box preferential rate of 10% for qualified industrial property royalty income, and Jeune Entreprise Innovante relief for eligible innovative companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no legal expiry for ordinary deficits; annual offset capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the remaining taxable profit exceeding that threshold; one-year carryback of up to EUR 1 million available)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: 2065-SD (Sociétés) – annual corporate income tax declaration, filed electronically through TéléTVA on impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year closing on 31 December: file no later than 3 May of the following year. For any other fiscal year end: file within three months of the fiscal close, with the standard administrative tolerance extended by fifteen days for required electronic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identifiers: SIREN number, APE/NAF classification (6202A / NAICS 541512 equivalent), legal form (SARL), registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must reflect the French permanent establishment address and local PEPE identifiers; a parent entity’s foreign registered office alone does not satisfy French filing domicile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax; adjustments for non-deductible expenses, exceptional costs, and intercompany recharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only French-source permanent establishment profit attributable to the French branch or PE; offshore service revenues must be allocated under the force of attraction principle where substance is located in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward amounts (report 209 CGI), deductible provisions, tax consolidation group relief where applicable, and reinvested long-term capital gains deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers may deduct only deficits economically connected with the French PE; foreign holding or foreign branch losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: research tax credit, innovation tax credit, employment-related credits, property restoration credits, and foreign tax credits; attach supporting schedule 2069-A.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit relief must be substantiated by the certificate of residence and OECD CRS relevant forms; DTA credits are applied on the French IS return, not as direct reductions in non-resident ancillary returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax at 25% standard rate and the 15% reduced band; computation of any social contribution, if applicable, and minimum tax (IFA) for previous deficits; no contribution sociale remains for 2024.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute IS solely on the PE taxable base; no French minimum tax applies if the PE proves no permanent establishment for the assessable year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% late-filing increase under Article 1728 CGI; a further 40% increase is applied if the return is not filed within 30 days after formal notice, and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres; late payment interest accrues at 0.4% per month (4.8% per annum).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: 2051-SD / 2052-SD (financial statement annexes to the 2065-SD) filed electronically via TéléTVA
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same as 2065-SD: 3 May for calendar-year closers; otherwise three months after fiscal year end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tangible and intangible fixed assets, software capitalisation, significant IT infrastructure, and amortisation pools.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate fixed assets to the French PE based on operational location; software assets held offshore but functionally used by the French ODC must be reported if title effectively remains in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 / Line 8 – Créances clients et dettes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intercompany accounts receivable/payable, trade debtors, accrued income, and related-party balance sheet items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign intercompany receivables and payables separately; non-arm’s-length balances attract transfer pricing recharacterisation and deemed interest under Article 212 CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue reclassified by business line; for the offshore development center, revenue derives from development, testing, maintenance, and software project management services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French PE operating revenues are taxed; remeasurement of intercompany invoicing at arm’s length; under Allocated Cost methodologies, the physical location of software engineers in France is decisive.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to produce the 2051/2052 schedules exposes the company to the same 10% to 80% late-filing increases and 0.4% monthly interest; administrative fines of up to EUR 100 per missing schedule may also apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident corporate shareholder must obtain a certificate of tax residence issued by its own tax administration and present it, together with a beneficial-owner statement, to the French paying agent before distribution. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an income tax treaty is invoked by using the applicable residence certificate and, where required, Form 5000 certification; excess withholding taxes are reclaimed through the annual corporate income tax return or by filing a specific reimbursement claim with the French local tax office.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory French withholding tax rate of 33.33% for intellectual property royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates are typically reduced to 0%, 5%, or 10%, depending on the jurisdiction and the IP class. Interest: statutory withholding is generally 0% for interest paid by a French company to unrelated non-resident creditors; treaties confirm 0% as the norm, but anti-abuse rules may impose a 25% withholding rate for non-arm’s-length interest instruments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million (annual turnover or total balance sheet assets) triggers mandatory transfer pricing documentation in France: Local File and Master File must be immediately producible; country-by-country reporting is additionally required when the multinational group consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 750 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a statutory Economic Substance Regulations return in the manner of offshore centres, but general law and anti-abuse jurisprudence require genuine economic substance. For an Offshore Development Center in a French SARL, substance is evidenced by locally based software engineers, payroll in France, premises physically occupied, local managerial decision-making, and commercial risk retention; artificial arrangements that strip profits to tax-favoured jurisdictions are recharacterised under Article L64 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales and OECD/ATAD principles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting taxable revenue from software license, development fees, and maintenance contracts; issuing fictitious invoices; recording intercompany offshore costs with no French operational substance; disguising distributions as compensation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% tax increase for bad faith under Article 1729 CGI, increased to 80% for abusive fraud (manœuvres frauduleuses); late-payment interest at 4.8% per annum; criminal fraude fiscale under Article 1741 CGI carries a fine of up to EUR 50,000 and two years’ imprisonment, with aggravated circumstances extending to EUR 100,000 and five years’ imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the company’s tax debt where fraud or negligent mismanagement is proven; civil restorative orders, personal asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment can follow a criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SARL as a mere invoicing shell that lacks actual software development capacity, with nominal employees, no management control, and all economic decisions taken by a foreign parent; transferring aggregated profit to zero-tax or low-tax entities without a valid business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative recharacterisation under Article L64 LPF; penalty of 80% of the reassessed tax; reversal of artificial legal acts; suspension of the benefit of DTA relief; publication of decisions; additional interest to apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing is applied where the corporate personality is entirely artificial; directors may be personally liable for hidden taxes, restitution of diverted profits, judicial exclusion from management, and criminal conviction for misuse of corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling corporate receipts through payment institutions such as Wise B2B, Payoneer, or wire transfers without maintaining proper AML/KYC files; concealing ultimate beneficial ownership; splitting invoices or repeatedly structuring payments to avoid French tax and banking thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Code Monétaire et Financier up to EUR 1,000,000 for legal persons; criminal penalties of up to five years’ imprisonment and fines up to EUR 375,000 for individuals; Tracfin referral and freezing of corporate bank accounts; failure to report beneficial ownership triggers separate penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for AML non-compliance, including civil damages, corporate asset freezing, travel restrictions, ineligibility to manage commercial companies, and criminal imprisonment where deliberate concealment is established.
